title: A notebook that reunites after a week offline
summary: Collect observations together even when nobody has a reliable connection.
opportunity: Build a fieldwork notebook where three people collect observations offline for seven days, then merge their notes with a clear explanation of conflicting edits and authorship.

title: Software that survives its own data format
summary: Let collaborators customize their tools without losing the ability to exchange information.
opportunity: Connect three independently evolving project trackers through reversible schema translations. Let a team rename or split fields without requiring every collaborator to upgrade at once.

title: Living diagrams that explain their assumptions
summary: Turn a model into something people can manipulate, question, and explain together.
opportunity: Build a diagram editor where a group can manipulate a model, inspect the assumptions behind each formula, compare alternatives, and publish a portable interactive explanation.

summary: Reshape a website around your own needs and share the adaptation with others.
opportunity: Let someone reorganize a difficult website using a spreadsheet view, save the adaptation locally, and share a recipe that explains the browser permissions it needs.

title: A workspace whose tools members can reshape
summary: Give a group room to change the software they use while they are using it.
opportunity: Build a workspace where a member can change a board or calculator directly, submit the change for review, and restore an earlier version without leaving the workspace.

summary: Keep your project profile and contribution record when you move to a different community.
opportunity: Store a builder's project profile and contribution records in their own data space. Demonstrate moving between two community applications without recreating the information or granting both applications permanent access.

title: Shared writing that preserves disagreement
summary: Let drafts converge while keeping competing explanations visible.
opportunity: Extend a collaborative editor so independently edited passages retain authorship, competing alternatives, and review decisions when writers merge their offline work.

summary: Let a community describe its work in a language that fits what it does.
opportunity: Give a makerspace a simple language for workshop recipes, with live feedback, examples, and a visual trace explaining how each instruction is interpreted.

title: Documents that become shared tools
summary: Let a useful document grow into an interactive tool as a group needs more from it.
opportunity: Start with a group's meeting document and let members turn part of it into an interactive decision board while preserving its history and shared editing.

opportunity: Build a visual automation editor for community operations where every block declares the data it reads, the changes it makes, and the permissions it needs, with a preview before execution.

title: A shared map of how a system might change
summary: Compare explanations of a system and see what follows from different assumptions.
opportunity: Let a group build a causal model, attach evidence and uncertainty to its connections, fork competing hypotheses, and compare what happens when an assumption changes.

existingWork: LOOPY already provides an interactive tool for thinking in systems. This proposal adds evidence, uncertainty, and a workflow for comparing competing models.

title: A neural network you can argue with
summary: Make a tiny neural network small enough to inspect and discuss together.
opportunity: Create a collaborative learning lab where people change a tiny neural network's inputs or weights, inspect the complete computation graph, and record competing explanations of its behavior.
